learn.title: A loop and an index
learn.body: An array and a `for` loop belong together. The loop variable is the index, and the body does the same thing to each element in turn. The standard shape is `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)`.

learn.title: Use < not <=
learn.body: With length `n` the valid indexes are 0 to `n - 1`. So the loop runs while `i < n`. Writing `i <= n` goes one step past the end, which is a bug we study in a later lesson.

learn.title: Add everything up
learn.body: The total is 3 + 9 + 4 + 7 = 23, and dividing by 4.0 gives the average 5.75. Using `4.0` avoids integer division.

learn.title: Find the biggest
learn.body: Start with the first element as the best so far. Then compare each of the others. It prints 9.

learn.title: Trace the sum
steps: i = 3: sum becomes 16 + 7 = 23, and the loop ends at i = 4

learn.body: Keep the length in a variable such as `n` instead of repeating the number 4 everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which loop visits every element of an array of length `n`?
questions.explanation: Start at 0 and stop before `n`. The others skip the first element or run one step too far.

questions.prompt: For `int v[] = {3, 9, 4, 7};`, what is the sum of all elements? Type the number.
What is `v[2]` in `int v[] = {3, 9, 4, 7};`? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Indexes start at 0: `v[0]` is 3, `v[1]` is 9, `v[2]` is 4.

questions.prompt: Why divide by `4.0` rather than `4` to get the average?
questions.explanation: Integer division would give 5 instead of 5.75.

questions.prompt: To find the biggest value, start with `max = v[\_\_]`.
questions.explanation: Using the first element as the starting best works for any numbers.

questions.prompt: How many elements of `{3, 9, 4, 7}` are greater than 5? Type the number.
Put the steps of finding a maximum in order.
steps: Set max to the first element
If it is bigger, update max
Repeat until the end of the array
questions.explanation: The best-so-far value is updated each time a bigger one shows up.
